definition: Space-based data centers or orbital AI infrastructure are proposed concepts to build AI data centers in the sun-synchronous orbit or other orbits using space-based solar power.
details: Space-based edge computing has historical roots in military architectures designed to bypass the latency of ground-based targeting networks. In the 1980s, the Strategic Defense Initiative's Brilliant Pebbles program first envisioned autonomous on-orbit data processing for missile defense. In 2019, the Space Development Agency (SDA) began to revive this decentralized approach through its Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA). This ambitious "sensor-to-shooter" infrastructure is treated as a prerequisite for the modern Golden Dome program, which would rely on space-based data processing to continuously track targets.

explainer.lead: Space-based data centers, or orbital AI infrastructure, are proposed concepts to build AI data centers in sun-synchronous or other orbits using space-based solar power. Their roots lie in military architectures designed to bypass ground-network latency.

tiers.eli5: The idea is to put AI computers in orbit, powered by sunlight, instead of on the ground.
tiers.practitioner: The concept traces to military interest in on-orbit processing, such as 1980s autonomous on-orbit data processing for missile defense, and later the SDA's Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture from 2019. Treat these as proposals, not deployed infrastructure.
tiers.paperLevel: Proposed concepts for AI data centers in sun-synchronous or other orbits powered by space-based solar power. No formal definition or bound is given.
